commands.name: cancel-agent-run
commands.description:
Cancel a run
Cancel a queued or running Agent run immediately without returning any results. You are billed for usage accrued before cancellation. If the run has already reached a terminal status, the API returns the existing run.

commands.name: create-agent-run
commands.description:
Create a run
Create an asynchronous Agent run. By default, the API returns the run object immediately. Set `Accept: text/event-stream` to stream run lifecycle events until the run reaches a terminal status.

options.name: --accept
options.description: Set to `text/event-stream` to receive server-sent events.

options.name: --exa-beta
options.description: Comma-separated beta feature tokens for opting into experimental features.

options.name: --input
options.description: Records to process and records or entities to exclude from the answer.

options.name: --metadata
options.description: Caller-provided metadata stored with the run.

options.name: --data-sources
options.description: Exa Connect data providers to enable for the run. Each entry enables all of that provider's tools.

options.name: --query
options.description: Natural-language question or instructions for the request.

options.name: --system-prompt
options.description: Additional instructions that guide generated output or agent behavior. Use this for source preferences, novelty constraints, duplication constraints, or other behavior guidance.

options.name: --effort
options.description: Cost and reasoning effort preference for the run. `auto` lets Exa choose the appropriate effort. `ultra` is the highest-effort tier for work where completeness and thoroughness matter more than latency or cost, including large list building, deep multi-source research, and criteria that are hard to verify.

options.name: --previous-run-id
options.description: Completed run ID to continue from. Must belong to the same team.

options.name: --user-identifier
options.description: An opaque ID your platform assigns to the end user this request is made for, such as a UUID. Lets Exa attribute usage to that end user rather than your whole team. Must not contain personal information such as an email address, phone number, username, or name. Hash such values before sending them. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. Retained even when your team has Zero Data Retention enabled. Does not affect results.

options.name: --budget-max-cost-dollars
options.description: Maximum amount this run can spend in US dollars. Accepts $1–$100 and applies only to `auto` and `ultra`; when omitted, the default cap is $5 for `auto` and $20 for `ultra`.

options.name: --budget-max-duration-seconds
options.description: Soft wall-clock ceiling for the run in seconds. Accepts 300–10,800 (5 minutes to 3 hours) and applies only to `ultra`. As the run approaches the limit, the agent stops starting new work and returns what it has found with `stopReason: "time_limit_reached"`.

Cancel a batch
Request cancellation of a batch. The batch stops scheduling new requests and drains in-flight work before settling to `cancelled`. Cancelling a batch that is already `cancelling` or `cancelled` is idempotent and returns the batch unchanged. A batch that has already reached a terminal status (`completed` or `expired`) cannot be cancelled and the request fails with a 409.

commands.name: search
commands.description:
Search
Perform a search with an Exa prompt-engineered query and retrieve a list of relevant results. Optionally get contents.

options.name: --moderation
options.description: Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --query
options.description: The query string for the search.

options.name: --type
options.description:
The search mode to use. Defaults to `auto`, a balanced mode recommended for most applications.
- `auto`: The default. A balanced mode that optimizes for both quality and speed and is recommended for most applications.
- `lite`: Low-cost, low-latency search for real-time and interactive experiences such as chat, voice agents, and autocomplete. Accepts only `query` (a single string), `objective`, `userIdentifier`, `metadata`, `category`, `numResults`, `contents.highlights`, `contents.text`, `contents.snapshotAsOf`, `userLocation`, `includeDomains`, `excludeDomains`, `startPublishedDate`, `endPublishedDate`, `moderation`, and `compliance`; a request that sets any other parameter is rejected. Serves cached content only; it never fetches live, so the freshness options are rejected.
- `deep-lite`: Performs lightweight research with synthesized results and a consistent 4-second latency, lower than full deep search.
- `deep`: Conducts comprehensive multi-step research with synthesis.
- `instant`: Legacy. Use `lite` instead. Runs a minimum-latency search that trades some search depth for speed. Unlike `lite`, it accepts every search parameter.
- `fast`: Legacy. Use `lite` instead. Runs a reduced-latency search for user-facing and interactive workflows. Unlike `lite`, it accepts every search parameter.
- `deep-reasoning`: Legacy. Use `deep` instead. Runs `deep` with stronger reasoning at each step, for complex analysis and decision-making tasks. For agentic, multi-step research, use the Agent API.

options.name: --objective
options.description: The broader goal this search serves: the task the caller is working on, beyond the query itself. When exposing this field to an agent as a tool parameter, describe it as: "Goal for this search turn; say which documents should rank first, which should be excluded, and what specific facts or figures to pull from them."
